title: Split async pipeline stages and introduce tokenized shedder for fine-grained backpressure
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Background: Multiple services report elevated tail latencies and burst-related failures in our async worker fleet. Root cause analysis shows a monolithic event-loop where intake, validation, dispatch, and execution share a common threadpool and retry path. This causes head-of-line blocking and unpredictable retry amplification when downstreams (Redis streams or Kafka partitions) flake. The current retry budget is coarse-grained and global, which makes it hard to protect high-priority customers or small fast requests from noisy noisy long-running jobs.

Goal: Decompose the current single worker loop into explicit, composable stages and add a tokenized shedder that enforces fine-grained backpressure by token budgets (per-customer, per-model, per-route). The refactor should reduce 99th percentile request latency under burst by at least 30% and cut duplicate retry events by >90% for transient downstream errors. It should also make retry semantics explicit and testable across Redis and Kafka adapters.
acceptance_criteria: New pipeline broken into intake -> validation -> dispatch -> execution -> ack/release stages with clear handoffs
Tokenized shedder implemented: configurable token buckets for customer/model/route and enforced in intake/dispatch
Retry path rewritten to use deterministic idempotency keys and dedup caches with TTLs, reducing duplicate work for transient errors
Adapters for Redis streams and Kafka consumer groups updated to surface partition-level pressure and to expose lease tokens
Per-stage bounded concurrency controls (executor pools) with metrics for queue depth, wait time, and token consumption
Automated stress test shows >=30% reduction in 99th percentile latency under simulated burst and >=90% reduction in duplicate retries
Migration plan executed with canary rollout and automatic fallback to legacy loop on regressions
Documentation updated: design doc, runbook, and developer guide for writing new pipeline stages
rollout_plan: 1) Land library-level abstractions for Stage and TokenShedder behind feature flag (no behavioral change)
2) Implement intake and validation stages and run integration tests against a staging Redis/Kafka cluster
3) Enable tokenized shedder in canary fleet (5% traffic), collect token metrics and adjust default budgets
4) Replace dispatch->execution in progressively larger cohorts (20% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback on error-rate or latency regressions
5) Remove legacy loop and merge telemetry-only flags after 2 weeks of stable 100% rollout
test_plan: Unit tests for Stage lifecycle: start, pause, resume, shutdown semantics
Property tests for TokenShedder under concurrent acceptance and token exhaustion
Integration tests against Redis Streams and Kafka: consumer rebalance, partition hot-spot, and lease loss scenarios
Chaos job: inject downstream latency and transient Redis/Kafka failures to ensure shedder drops low-priority tokens instead of stalling high-priority work
Load test: bursty arrival patterns using our ingress replay harness to validate 99p latency and retry de-duplication targets
comments: 2026-02-11: Initial triage complete. Confirmed head-of-line blocking reproduces locally with synthetic burst harness. (Sofia)
2026-02-18: Spike finished: Stage interface prototype implemented and evaluated. Observed 15% 99p improvement when using separate executors for validation vs execution. (Aaron)

2026-02-28: Design review with Platform and Observability: agreed on tokenized shedder semantics and required metrics (token_consumed, token_rejected, per_route_backlog). Action: add shedder metrics to telemetry spec. (Sofia, Priya)
2026-03-05: Implemented idempotency key generator for retry path. Integration tests show dedup cache reduces duplicate replays in transient 503 scenario. Need TTL tuning. (Aaron)

2026-03-09: Canary enabled at 5% traffic. Token budgets initially too low for some customers — bumped defaults and added per-customer override API. Observability dashboards showing expected token burn. (Sofia)
2026-03-12: Mid-canary checkpoint: no increase in error budget, 99p latency down ~28% in canary cohort. Proceeding with staged rollout. (Aaron)
